title: Doge discovers the stupidest study ever with the government that blows $ 1.2 million … to discover it obvious
text:
A doge legislator blows the whistle at more than $ 1.2 million in federal funds spent on studying the drinking and sex habits of Super Bowl Watchers.
The Ministry of Government Efficiency of Elon Musk (DOGE) has worked to discover federal waste and to delete from federal balance sheets.
This week, DOGE claims that the federal subscriptions on the New York Times have canceled, the financing for diversity, shares and inclusion (dei) has cut off initiatives and has terminated millions in advisory contracts.
During these reviews, Senate Doge Caucus chairman Joni Ernst (R-IOWA) came some shocking Super Bowl-related editions by prior to the big match of this weekend between the Kansas City Chiefs and the Philadelphia Eagles in New Orleans.
‘We focused on the Super Bowl, and what we have seen is about $ 1.2 million issued by the National Institutes of Health on a few studies to find out if there is more Binge Drink on Super Bowl Sunday, and then as There is a baby boom nine months later in the winning team city, “Ernst told DailyMail.com.
These striking National Institute of Health (NIH) projects were strictly approved to determine the health results after the Super Bowl.
A study from 2017 entitled ‘Super Bowl Babies’: Do Counties with Super Bowl winning teams experienced an increase in births’ received no less than $ 710,000 dollars from NIH nine months later.
The other shocking scientific study published in 2014 was entitled ‘Super Bowl Sunday: Risky Business for Risk (male) drinkers’ and received $ 563,800.
The NIH has spent more than $ 563,000 to determine whether heavy drinkers consume more alcohol on Super Bowl Sunday than every Saturday evening. The results showed that they drank two more drinks during the Super Bowl than on Saturday
Another NIH study that cost $ 710,000 to determine whether more babies are born in the Super Bowl -winning team of the Super Bowl. The results showed that there was no pattern of raised births in super bowl-winning areas
Senate Doge Caucus chairman Joni Ernst has assessed government spending and in search of areas to lower waste. During the research of her team they came across two super bowl studies
“So I think they try to find out if people are really, very happy after celebrating,” Ernst joked.
But the enormous amount of money spent on the study is not a joke, she added.
The Republican wondered ‘ If there is a certain draw at a university or someone’s Alma Mater, “who could have led to such surprising expenditures being distributed.
‘The nih, maybe they just think, well, we have the money, so we’re going to spend it. Well, what I would say now is, I am sorry that you no longer get that money because you waste it. ‘
“Why do we spend tax dollars here?” Ernst went on. “I can’t understand what the good is for the American people.”
However, the results of the studies finds are just as shocking than the actual expenditure.
The Baby Boom study of $ 710,000 was a total failure.
It discovered that there was no consistent pattern of raised births in the provinces where the super bowl -winning teams were.

In the meantime, the drinking study discovered that men who drink a lot tend to drink more on Super Bowl Sunday than their average Saturday.
The study even showed that these men drank on average two to three more alcoholic beverages than usual during the big game.
“These findings suggest that heavy drinking during the Super Bowl (and in collaboration with other sporting events), in particular among men, justifies extra attention because of the potential for harmful consequences for public health,” the study found.
In essence, NIH has spent more than half a million dollars to confirm that, yes, men drink more alcohol on Super Bowl Sunday.
